title: [Feature] Enable fused RMSNorm+cast capability for Atlas A2
body:
## Summary

Enable the existing fused `npu_rms_norm_cast` operator on Atlas A2 by exposing
`HardwareCapability.RMS_NORM_CAST` in the A2 hardware profile.

The kernel already has `ascend910b` build artifacts (`csrc/moe/rms_norm_cast`),
but the capability was A3-only. As a result, A2 used the fallback
`RMSNorm` + `.float()`, which runs two kernels and round-trips the normalized
BF16 tensor through HBM.

DSV4.1 consumes the FP32 normalized hidden state as the MoE router input
(`DeepseekV41DecoderLayer.rms_norm_cast`), so this fallback runs once per layer.

## Change

- `vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py`: add `RMS_NORM_CAST` to the A2
  capability set and update the capability comment.
- `tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py`: update the expected A2 capability
  set.
- `tests/ut/device/test_device_op.py`: expect the fused operator on A2 when
  custom ops are enabled.

No kernel source changes.

## Validation

Hardware: Atlas 800 A2 / 910B4 (32 GB HBM), CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10.0+cpu,
torch_npu 2.10.0.post4.

Microbenchmark, hidden=5120, BF16 (fused `npu_rms_norm_cast` vs
`npu_rms_norm(...).float()`):

| tokens | eager fused | eager fallback | ACL graph fused | ACL graph fallback |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.045 ms | 0.088 ms | 0.0125 ms | 0.0123 ms |
| 256 | 0.048 ms | 0.091 ms | 0.0281 ms | 0.0324 ms |
| 4096 | 0.269 ms | 0.281 ms | 0.2795 ms | 0.3086 ms |

- Eager: ~1.9x at small T, ~1.05x at T=4096.
- ACL graph: T=1 is neutral (within noise); ~15% at T=256 and ~10% at T=4096.
- The op is ACL-graph capturable.

Operator consistency:

- `pytest tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py -q` -> 12 passed.
- `pytest tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_rms_norm_cast.py -q`
  -> 8 passed on 910B4 (FP16/BF16, hidden=7168, T=1/16/128, including the NPU
  graph test).
- The fused FP32 output matches `npu_rms_norm(...).float()` exactly; the
  existing e2e test asserts `actual_fp32 == actual.float()` with rtol=0/atol=0.

## Notes

- `npu_rms_norm_cast` requires `gamma` to have the same dtype as `x`; the
  model RMSNorm weight is BF16, so the A2 path is valid. FP32 gamma paths must
  cast or keep the fallback.
- This PR only changes the capability gate; it does not touch the kernel.
- The e2e coverage already exercises the fused op directly; this PR makes the
  model path use it on A2.

## Validation after updating main (2026-10-26)

The branch was updated onto main `06aac4532`. The sampling
cleanup in #19393 removed `NPU_TOP_K_TOP_P`; this PR preserves that removal
and adds only `RMS_NORM_CAST` to the A2 capability set and its test expectation.

- The CI checkout's `git rebase BASE_SHA` command passed locally. A forced
  replay of the commit also passed and produced the same file tree.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` passed.
- 17 CPU cases for hardware profiles and RMSNorm dispatch passed with temporary
  import isolation for the unavailable vLLM/CANN dependencies. The three Python feature
  files are unchanged from that validation.
- The Dynamo test fails on the local PyTorch 2.7.0 runtime because it cannot
  trace `frozenset.__contains__`. The same failure was reproduced against
  unmodified main; this PR does not change that path.
- The earlier A2 operator results above predate this update. No kernel code was
  changed and no new NPU run was performed.

## Test plan

- CI unit tests.
- A2 e2e `test_rms_norm_cast`.
- DSV4.1 op-level tests on A2 (full-model validation requires the documented
  4-node A2 pool).

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
